title: Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check
objectives: Apply the module's compliance rules to any overlap recommendation.
Pass the trainer's final check: explain, measure and fix overlap, and handle “more funds is safer” within compliance.
body_md:
Do: check overlap before recommending any new fund. Base consolidation on the client's goals, risk profile and costs. Explain exit loads and that redemptions may be taxed; refer tax to a CA. Use overlap data from published portfolios and name the date. Record reasons for each fund kept or dropped, with client approval.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Check overlap before recommending any new fund | Add funds to a portfolio without checking what it already holds |
| Base consolidation on the client's goals, risk profile and costs | Recommend switches mainly to earn commission or move assets to one AMC |
| Explain exit loads and that redemptions may be taxed; refer tax to a CA | Give tax advice or ignore switching costs |
| Use overlap data from published portfolios and name the date | Claim a fund is “better” without a fair, like-for-like comparison |
| Record reasons for each fund kept or dropped, with client approval | Redeem or switch without documented consent |

> **Investor takeaway:** Standard disclaimer: mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully. Past performance does not guarantee future returns. Final check for trainers: a new joiner passes this module when they can explain what portfolio overlap is and why it happens; measure overlap between two funds and read an overlap tool's output; judge when overlap is a real problem and when it is acceptable; consolidate a cluttered portfolio into a simple core-and-satellite structure; check the cost of switching before recommending any change; and handle the “more funds is safer” belief, within compliance.
example: A trainee measures overlap from published portfolios, names the date, checks loads and tax, and records keep/drop reasons with approval.
say: Use overlap data from published portfolios and name the date.
Record reasons for each fund kept or dropped, with approval.
never: Claim a fund is “better” without a fair comparison.
Redeem or switch without documented consent.
